item.title: Den Den Town: Osaka's Electronics and Anime District — Guide
item.description: Den Den Town, in the Nipponbashi district south of Namba, is Osaka’s centre for electronics, anime and otaku culture — the city’s counterpart to Tokyo’s Akihabara. Once a strip of radio and electrical-parts shops, it has evolved into blocks packed with anime and manga stores, retro and current video games, figures, trading cards, hobby and model shops, alongside maid cafes and specialist retailers of every niche. It is less polished and less crowded than Akihabara but rewarding for collectors, and each spring the streets host the Nipponbashi Street Festa, one of Japan’s largest cosplay events.

item.title: Kuromon Ichiba Market Guide: Osaka's Kitchen, Stall by Stall
item.description: Known as “Osaka’s Kitchen,” Kuromon Ichiba has fed the city for nearly 200 years — a 600-metre covered arcade of around 150 stalls and shops selling the freshest seafood, wagyu, fruit, pickles, and street snacks in Minami. Once the wholesale market that supplied Osaka’s restaurants, it’s now equal parts working market and food-lover’s playground: vendors grill scallops and fugu to order, slice tuna sashimi before your eyes, and torch wagyu skewers at the counter.
